title: Chirped thickness stack to broaden visible reflection band
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped multilayer stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses will achieve more uniform reflectance across 400-700 nm than a periodic stack, at the cost of slightly reduced peak reflectance, while maintaining transmission at 1530-1565 nm.
design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflectors vary the optical thickness of layers across the stack, creating multiple overlapping stopbands that merge into a broader reflection band. By grading thickness from values appropriate for 400 nm at one end to 700 nm at the other, the full visible band can be covered.
proposed_topology: Air | hfo2(1), sio2(1), hfo2(2), sio2(2), ..., hfo2(15), sio2(15) | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers with chirped thicknesses
design_variables: layer thicknesses with chirp parameter controlling thickness gradient across the 30 layers
soft_objectives: maximize minimum reflectance across 400-700 nm band
maintain smooth thickness progression to aid manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped designs require precise thickness control per layer
Thickness gradient may increase deposition time
HfO2/SiO2 stress balance must be maintained across varying thicknesses
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method with non-periodic structures
expected_advantages: Broader reflection band than periodic stack
Better coverage at band edges (400 nm, 700 nm)
Thickness gradient provides additional optimization degrees of freedom
known_risks: Chirp may introduce transmission ripples in the 1530-1565 nm band
Optimization landscape may be more complex with chirp parameter
Manufacturing tolerance may be tighter for non-uniform thicknesses
execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer chirped multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with hfo2, for 30 total layers. Layer thicknesses follow a chirped progression where optical thickness varies systematically from layer 1 to layer 30 to cover 400-700 nm reflection band. Optimize the chirp parameter and individual layer thickness deviations to maximize reflectance uniformity in 400-700 nm and transmittance in 1530-1565 nm. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.
